text:
Two springs in a row, these teams met with the Stanley Cup on the line and Florida won both times. On Tuesday the Oilers walked into Sunrise and made it look easy for two periods, winning 5-2 for their sixth straight victory. Along the way Connor McDavid broke Wayne Gretzky's Oilers record for power-play points, as Oilersnation noted, which is the kind of footnote that only sounds small until you remember whose name it replaced.

Edmonton did not have the puck much. Florida had 55 shot attempts to 32, and at even strength the chances were close to level (1.20 expected goals for Florida, 1.09 for Edmonton; expected goals measure the quality of the looks). The game was decided on special teams and in the crease. The Oilers went 2 for 4 on the power play, worth 1.42 expected goals on its own, while Florida went 0 for 2.

Kasperi Kapanen opened the scoring at 9:57 of the first, McDavid made it 2-0 on the power play off a 55% chance, and Vasily Podkolzin scored twice in the second, once at even strength and once with the man advantage, both with Leon Draisaitl assisting. Podkolzin finished with two goals and an assist and was the night's first star. Zach Hyman did not score but kept finding the dangerous ice: his own chances added up to 1.02 expected goals, including a 40% look in the first that went wide.

At the other end Devon Levi stopped 20 of 22, slightly better than expected, and led everyone in the game in wins added. The headlines have been asking for two weeks whether he is the goalie Edmonton has been searching for; nights like this keep the question open in the best way. Jacob Markstrom allowed four on 17 shots, 1.5 more than those shots deserved.

Matthew Tkachuk scored twice in the third, one on a shot with under a 1% chance, to make the final ten minutes interesting, and Draisaitl closed it with a backhand at 19:27. Florida is still waiting on Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, and without them the Panthers looked like a team that can hit you all night (39 hits) without hurting you.
headline: Oilers win six straight as McDavid takes a Gretzky record
